spacertales-alembrine-history.label: Alembrine
spacertales-alembrine-history.title: Alembrine: the second use of a harvest
spacertales-alembrine-history.body:
Alembrine began with vessel and pipe work for small fermenting shops. The name recalls an alembic, an old kind of still. Customers cared less about the word than about equipment they could keep clean, supplied and working in limited space. Copper and brass made the firm's equipment easy to distinguish from the rest of a process room.

The Phobos' Alembrine Copperhead-3 Fermenter-Still joined the vessels into a supported production job. The Corker-2 Bottling Unit gave suitable cask ethanol another route into bottled spirit. Both require actual supplies. A still does not make a harvest surplus merely because a customer would like a drink.

Some of Alembrine's earliest orders came from customers already using Verdemorrow equipment. The makers' publicity calls this a natural partnership. Crews call it an argument over whether the grain belongs to supper, planting stock or the still. The correct answer changes with the person holding the invoice.

A dealer once described Alembrine spirit as essential voyage provision. The firm's technical staff asked for the phrase to be removed from an equipment leaflet. The dealer moved it to an advert. Alembrine has since tried to distinguish the process business from the stories people tell about its bottles.

Alembrine's correspondence desk separates equipment questions from the social uses of its product. Service letters name feed, vessels and bottling supplies. Customer letters concern gifts, favours and whose turn it is to pay. Filing them together does not make them the same business.

spacertales-slingwright-history.label: Slingwright
spacertales-slingwright-history.title: Slingwright: the load that remained
spacertales-slingwright-history.body:
Slingwright's first customers were small processing crews who discovered that a profitable batch still left material aboard. Recovery machinery gave the remainder a name. Storage gave it a location. Neither necessarily gave it a departure.

The Phobos' Slingwright RM-1 Reaction Mass Feeder supplies a supported route for declared terminal remainders into reaction mass. It is a dedicated powered job with accepted feed, not an invitation to throw every object aboard into the thrusters. Useful feed still belongs in its useful process when that is the better choice.

A feeder brochure has room for a machine and a short description. A working plant needs room for the accepted stock and for the person supplying it. Slingwright's service literature discusses that space more plainly than its sales photographs. Crews read both before agreeing to a refit.

The company's name joins sling and wright: a maker of something that throws. Sales staff have tried giving it a grander origin. Crew prefer the shorter one.

Independent operators usually discover Slingwright after discovering the storage bill for the rest of their plant. Large contractors tend to discover it after receiving a complaint about the crew's growing tomorrow pile. Both ask whether they can keep the output and send somebody else the leftovers.

spacertales-galley-process-boundary.label: Grain, seed and the still
spacertales-galley-process-boundary.title: Three claims on one cupboard
spacertales-galley-process-boundary.body:
A ship that grows food and runs an Alembrine still has more uses for produce than it had before buying either machine. A portion may be supper, stock for another planting or feed for a supported process. It cannot serve every purpose at once.

Aboard independent ships the argument is usually small and immediate. The person tending a crop wants a reserve. The cook wants a meal. The owner sees a market price. Someone else sees a bottle at the end of the next shift. Each can explain why their use is reasonable.

Verdemorrow and Alembrine advertisements make the combination look inevitable. A working crew decides what can actually be spared. There is nothing self-sustaining about a cupboard nobody is allowed to open.

Old galley labels survive beside new process labels. FOOD, SEED and STILL can look much alike after a few damp fingers and an impatient rewrite. The most successful compromise is often three separate places and a cook who knows where they are.

spacertales-alembrine-pump-story.title: The borrowed pump
text: At [place], Alembrine dealers are debating two incompatible accounts of a promotional bottle sent to settle a disagreement over a borrowed pump. One account says the bottle reconciled the owners; the other says it arrived at the wrong ship and widened the quarrel. The firm says neither account came from its process department. The pump's owner says any correction should include the pump's current location.

Two accounts of a promotional bottle are going round Alembrine dealers at [place]. It was sent to settle an argument over a borrowed pump: one account says it made peace between the owners, the other that it reached the wrong ship and made things worse. Alembrine says neither came from its process department. The pump's owner wants any correction to say where the pump is now.
mention: That Alembrine bottle either fixed the pump argument or started it. Nobody's found the pump.
Either that Alembrine bottle settled the pump quarrel or it made it worse. The pump is still missing.

spacertales-alembrine-provision-word.title: Voyage provision
text: At [place], Alembrine has asked an equipment dealer to separate spirit advertising from its operating leaflet. The dealer had described bottled spirit as essential voyage provision next to the fermenter specifications. The firm's technical staff say the machine requires feed and proper process supplies, while a crew's essential provisions include meals. The dealer says meals were outside the campaign's scope.

Alembrine has asked a dealer at [place] to keep spirit advertising out of its operating leaflet, after the dealer called bottled spirit essential voyage provision beside the fermenter specifications. The machine needs feed and proper process supplies, technical staff say; a crew's essential provisions include meals. The dealer says meals were outside the campaign.
mention: Alembrine's still leaflet accidentally made the spirit sound like supper. Cook might disagree.
An Alembrine leaflet called spirit essential provisions. The cook has views on what's essential.

spacertales-alembrine-grain-dispute.title: The cupboard meeting
text: At [place], a joint Verdemorrow and Alembrine display has been delayed after its host crew used the demonstration grain for a hot meal. Dealers say the intended demonstration was a complete shipboard supply chain. The cook says the grain completed one. The next display will reserve separate stocks for planting, cooking and process feed.

A joint Verdemorrow and Alembrine display at [place] is running late because its host crew cooked the demonstration grain. Dealers had planned to show a complete shipboard supply chain; the cook says the grain completed one. Next time, planting stock, cooking grain and process feed will be kept apart.
mention: They cooked the grain for that Verdemorrow and Alembrine display. Sounds like a successful demonstration to me.
The display grain ended up as supper. Depending who you ask, the demonstration worked.

spacertales-slingwright-worker-photo.title: Somebody still loads it
text: The Slingwright desk at [place] has retrieved a worker's letter about an RM-1 publicity photograph. The writer supplied the loading that left the room clear, but the caption credited the feeder alone. Sales filed the complaint as an image correction. The desk is separating the equipment claim from the disputed fee; no payment has been reported.

A worker's letter about an RM-1 publicity photograph has been retrieved by the Slingwright desk at [place]. The writer did the loading that left the room clear; the caption credited only the feeder. Sales filed the complaint as an image correction. The desk is separating the equipment claim from the disputed fee, and no payment has been reported.
mention: Slingwright's letter at [place] counts the worker who loaded the feeder. The fee is still another question.
That Slingwright letter at [place] gives the loader some credit at last. Nobody has paid the fee yet.

spacertales-slingwright-valuable-stock.title: A useful distinction
text: At [place], a Slingwright dealer has withdrawn advice to send all processing output to the reaction-mass feeder. Operators pointed out that finished material and useful feed have other purposes, while the RM-1 has a defined list of terminal remainders it accepts. The dealer says all was intended informally. Customers say their invoices are rather formal.

Advice to send all processing output to the reaction-mass feeder has been withdrawn by a Slingwright dealer at [place]. Operators pointed out that finished material and useful feed have other uses, and the RM-1 accepts only a defined list of terminal remainders. The dealer meant all informally; customers say their invoices are rather formal.
mention: Slingwright dealer said throw all the output in the feeder. Apparently all was only advertising.
A Slingwright dealer told folk to feed everything to the RM-1. The feeder itself is pickier than that.

spacertales-alembrine-letter-call.title: Labels wanted, bottles kept
text: Alembrine's customer letters desk at [place] is comparing old product descriptions with current bottled stock. Operators with a Copperhead-3 are invited to read the correspondence. A present bottle can help identify a label, but will not be taken or treated as proof of an old batch.

At [place], Alembrine's customer letters desk is checking old product descriptions against current bottled stock, and invites Copperhead-3 operators to read the correspondence. A bottle on hand can help identify a label; it will not be taken, and it proves nothing about an old batch.
mention: Alembrine's desk at [place] is comparing labels. Keeping your bottle sounds like the useful part.
Alembrine wants Copperhead-3 owners to read some old letters at [place]. You keep your bottle.

spacertales-slingwright-letter-call.title: Loading belongs in the picture
text: The Slingwright correspondence desk at [place] has asked RM-1 operators to read a retained worker's account of equipment publicity. The desk wants loading work described alongside the feeder's accepted stock. It is offering a copy of the letters, not a job, a payment or a request to run a batch.

RM-1 operators are invited by the Slingwright correspondence desk at [place] to read a worker's account of equipment publicity, kept so that the loading work is described alongside the feeder's accepted stock. The desk offers copies of the letters only: no job, no payment and no batch to run.
mention: Slingwright has loading letters at [place]. Reading them won't use up your feed.
There are loading letters at the Slingwright desk at [place]. Read them; nobody's asking for a batch.

text:
Phobos' Alembrine Copperhead-3 Fermenter-Still
A second use for supported feed you can spare. A proper process, real supplies and cask storage planned around the result. Decide what belongs to supper before starting.

Phobos' Alembrine Copperhead-3 Fermenter-Still
Supported feed you can spare, given a second life. A proper process, real supplies and cask storage planned for the result. Settle what belongs to supper before you start.

Phobos' Alembrine Corker-2 Bottling Unit
Suitable cask ethanol into Alembrine spirit, with the required bottling supplies. Give the product a label and give the cook a different cupboard.

Phobos' Alembrine Corker-2 Bottling Unit
Suitable cask ethanol, the right bottling supplies, and Alembrine spirit at the end of it. Label every bottle, and keep them in a different cupboard from the cook's.

Alembrine
Copper, brass and the end of a long shift. Process equipment for the feed you have actually set aside. Meals, planting stock and process feed deserve their own places.

Alembrine
Copper, brass and a long shift finally over. Process equipment for feed you have truly set aside; meals, planting stock and process feed each keep their own shelf.

Phobos' Slingwright RM-1 Reaction Mass Feeder
The remainder still weighs something. Give accepted terminal remainder stock its supported route into reaction mass. Powered machinery; somebody still has to supply the feed.

Phobos' Slingwright RM-1 Reaction Mass Feeder
Remainders still have mass. Send accepted terminal remainder stock along its supported route into reaction mass. Powered machinery, and someone still has to keep it fed.

line: The bottle made it back. The borrowed pump didn't. That's the Alembrine story I believe.
Of all the Alembrine stories, I trust the one where the bottle came home and the pump never did.
Bottle returned, pump still out on loan. Sounds like every borrowing I've heard of.
Cook caught a dealer carrying our grain towards the still. Called the whole demonstration supper and took it back.
A dealer tried to take our grain to the still. Cook stepped in, called it supper, and that was that.
Our cook rescued the grain from a still demonstration. The dealer never saw it again, except on a plate.
Food, planting stock, process feed. Same cupboard doesn't mean the same use.
Three piles: eat it, plant it, or process it. Mixing them up wastes all three.
Grain for supper, grain for sowing, grain for the still. Label which is which.
Alembrine gives the end of a shift a bottle. The captain gives it another shift.
End of shift: Alembrine offers a bottle. The captain offers overtime.
The still gives us a reason to stop. The captain gives us a reason not to.
Never open the first bottle until the batch is put away. That's what the brewer says when he wants you to help tidy up.
First bottle stays shut until the batch is stowed. Funny how that rule always gets you tidying.
Never toast a batch before it's put away. Bad luck, says the brewer. Free labour, I say.
I'm less worried about the still than the argument over what grain we're allowed to put in it.
The still's fine. What worries me is the row about which grain goes in it.
We'll argue over the grain long before the still gives us trouble.
That Alembrine leaflet called spirit voyage provision. The cook deserves a chance to read the next draft.
Spirit as voyage provision? Let the cook edit that leaflet next time.
Whoever wrote that Alembrine leaflet should spend a week living on its idea of provisions.
Bought a feeder for the tomorrow pile. Now the tomorrow pile is waiting to be loaded.
We bought a feeder to clear the tomorrow pile. The pile has learned to wait for the feeder.
The feeder eats the leftovers. Somebody still has to carry them over, and it's always tomorrow.
Last plant I worked had a Slingwright feeder bought after every store was full. I've seen better orders of work.
Worked a plant that bought its Slingwright feeder only after every store was stuffed. A bit late, that.
My old plant got a feeder once the stores were full to the hatch. Planning was not our strong point.
Finished stock is not automatically remainder feed. Read what the feeder accepts before moving the crate.
Don't send good stock to the feeder. It takes remainders from a list; check the list first.
The RM-1 has a list. Finished goods aren't on it.
When does leftover become waste? When nobody wants it, or when nobody will pay to store it?
Is it leftover or waste? Depends whether anybody will pay to keep it.
At what point does spare become rubbish: when no one wants it, or when storing it costs more than it's worth?
Port charges storage on remainder stock. Seems the one thing a batch makes reliably is another bill.
Storage fees on the remainders. Every batch makes at least one product, and it's always a bill.
Port wants rent for our leftovers. The leftovers are the only thing that never runs short.

spacertales-alembrine-pump-lore.text: Alembrine keeps customer correspondence separately from process records. A bottle may carry an apology or a favour; its label cannot prove that either reached the right person.

spacertales-alembrine-three-cupboards.text: Ships running both Verdemorrow and Alembrine equipment tend to invent three labels early: food, planting stock and process feed. Arguments survive even good labels.

spacertales-slingwright-load-history.text: Slingwright sells a route for accepted remainder stock, not a pair of hands. Working crews allow room for loading when they allow room for a feeder.
